name: Voyager
summary: NASA planetary and interstellar mission series. Its direct dark-matter connection is external reanalysis of Voyager 1's combined electron / positron flux beyond the heliopause, constraining MeV particle dark matter and evaporating primordial black holes. The spacecraft were not designed specifically for dark matter.
physics_targets: MeV–sub-GeV dark-matter annihilation or decay into electrons and positrons
Hawking radiation from primordial black holes
detection_principle: The CRS electron telescope measures penetrating-particle energy deposits with solid-state detectors and tungsten absorber layers of different thicknesses. Beyond the heliopause, Voyager 1 measures a combined low-energy electron / positron spectrum without the strong suppression from near-Earth solar modulation. External analyses compare it with propagated dark-matter-product spectra. The instrument does not distinguish electrons from positrons event by event.

sites.name: Voyager 1 / 2 in deep space and the local interstellar medium
sites.location: The spacecraft follow different deep-space trajectories; dark-matter reanalyses mainly use Voyager 1 data beyond the heliopause

status.label: Mission continuing; key historical particle instruments have been switched off
status.evidence: NASA's instrument page records Voyager 1 CRS shutdown on 2025-02-25; JPL records LECP shutdown on 2026-04-17 to extend the mission. The Voyager 2 CRS page says it remains on with shutdown planned in 2026; the plan is not treated here as completed.

timeline.event: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause, entering the interstellar cosmic-ray environment used in the dark-matter analyses cited here.
Published MeV dark-matter limits using Voyager 1 / AMS-02.
Published primordial-black-hole dark-matter constraints from the Voyager 1 electron–positron spectrum.
NASA's instrument page records Voyager 1 CRS shutdown to conserve power.
Voyager 1 LECP switched off to extend the spacecraft mission.

collaboration.name: NASA Voyager mission / CRS instrument team; independent DM reanalyses
collaboration.participants_note: Distinguish the spacecraft and CRS teams, authors of the original cosmic-ray measurements, and independent researchers such as Boudaud et al. who performed dark-matter interpretations; this is not a separate NASA dark-matter-search collaboration.

key_parameters.name: CRS nominal electron science band
key_parameters.value: 3–110 MeV; the original interstellar spectrum reaches about 2.7 MeV

key_parameters.name: TET structure
key_parameters.value: 8 solid-state detectors, each 3 mm thick and 4.5 cm² in area, interleaved with tungsten absorbers of different thicknesses

key_parameters.name: Electron / positron separation
key_parameters.value: CRS does not resolve charge sign; dark-matter analyses use the combined e−+e+ flux

phases.name: Planetary exploration and interstellar mission
phases.description: The spacecraft series continues Solar-System / interstellar science; dark-matter research was not an original mission objective.

phases.name: Historical Voyager 1 CRS cosmic-ray data
phases.description: CRS was switched off in 2025, but previously acquired data remain available for dark-matter reanalysis.

phases.name: Voyager2 CRS
phases.description: NASA's page records the instrument as on, with shutdown planned in 2026; the final execution date was not verified in this review.

results.summary: Independent analyses constrain MeV dark-matter annihilation / decay using the low-energy cosmic-ray spectrum beyond the heliopause and extend mass coverage jointly with AMS-02. Limits depend on propagation and the assumed final state.

The Voyager 1 spectrum constrains the dark-matter fraction in evaporating primordial black holes. Under the paper's model, PBHs below 10^16 g contribute less than about 0.1%; this is not an exclusion across all PBH masses.

science_scope: Classified here as indirect detection through cosmic-ray products, even though particles are counted directly aboard the spacecraft. Dark-matter constraints come from external reanalysis of real cosmic-ray data, not from the spacecraft measuring dark-matter particles.
